description: Test your knowledge of Head & neck Joints, Histology, Development, Radiography & Surface marking.

cards.text: What type of joint is the atlantooccipital joint, and what movements does it allow?
cards.answer: Synovial ellipsoid (condyloid) joint allowing nodding (flexion/extension) and small lateral flexion, but NO rotation.

cards.text: Describe the atlantoaxial joint and its characteristic movement.
cards.answer: Three joints (two lateral synovial + median joint with dens); allows rotation of 40-45° each side, contributing 50% of total cervical rotation.

tip.tip: "No movement" (shaking head) = atlantoaxial; rotation IS the primary function

cards.text: What is the clinical significance of the transverse ligament of atlas?
cards.answer: It is the most critical stabilizing structure holding the dens against the anterior arch; rupture causes spinal cord compression risk and requires immediate neurosurgical intervention.

tip.tip: Transverse ligament = the key keeper preventing dens from compressing cord

cards.text: What are normal atlantoaxial interval (ADI) measurements, and what does >3mm indicate?
cards.answer: Adults: ≤3mm; Children: ≤5mm. ADI >3mm in adults indicates transverse ligament rupture or laxity—immediate neurosurgical concern.

tip.tip: "3-5 rule": 3mm is max in adults, 5mm in children

cards.text: Why do Down syndrome patients need cervical X-ray screening before contact sports?
cards.answer: Down syndrome causes connective tissue hypotonia leading to transverse ligament laxity and atlantoaxial instability, risking spinal cord injury with contact.

tip.tip: Down syndrome + lax ligaments = cervical clearance mandatory

cards.text: What are the key histological features of the thyroid gland?
cards.answer: Spherical follicles with eosinophilic colloid (thyroglobulin) surrounded by cuboidal-columnar follicular cells; parafollicular C cells secrete calcitonin.

tip.tip: Pink colloid inside follicles = thyroid ID feature

cards.text: How do you distinguish parathyroid from thyroid histologically?
cards.answer: Parathyroid has densely packed chief cells (dark) with scattered oxyphil cells (pink) and minimal stroma; lacks thyroid's follicular structure and colloid.

cards.text: What are the distinguishing histological features of anterior versus posterior pituitary?
cards.answer: Anterior lobe is cellular with color variation (acidophils and basophils); posterior lobe is pale and paucicellular with Herring bodies storing ADH and oxytocin.

tip.tip: Anterior = colorful cells; Posterior = pale with Herring bodies
